rules.intentionally_uncovered_reason: Architectural invariant: not falsifiable by a data-driven fixture. Enforced by the typed encode(shape, value) API surface and the Phase 1 no-reflection / no-Any self-checks (docs/implementation/phase-01-canonical-encoding.md section 5).
rules.short_statement: Encoding is schema-directed: the encoder is driven by an explicit machine type (Shape) and never reflects over arbitrary host objects.
Canonical bytes are UTF-8 without BOM, contain no insignificant whitespace and have no leading or trailing data; decoders reject all of these.
Machine numerics are encoded as canonical decimal (or float64 hex) text inside JSON strings; JSON numbers are never the canonical authority and are rejected by the decoder.
String content is NFC-normalized: canonically equivalent inputs produce identical canonical bytes, and the decoder rejects non-NFC text.
Map keys are NFC-normalized before use.
Map keys and record members are emitted in unsigned UTF-8 byte lexicographic order; input order never affects canonical bytes.
Duplicate map keys are rejected, including keys that collide only after NFC normalization; never last-write-wins.
float64 is encoded as exactly 16 lowercase IEEE-754 hex characters inside a JSON string (big-endian bit pattern).
NaN and infinities are rejected by both encoder and decoder.
The float64 -0 bit pattern canonicalizes to +0; the decoder rejects the -0 pattern as non-canonical.
bytes are unpadded base64url; padding, the standard alphabet, impossible lengths and non-canonical trailing bits are rejected.
timestamp and duration are nominal int64 microsecond values encoded as canonical int64 text; cross-assignment between them and int64 is rejected.
Option is explicitly tagged: None encodes {"none":null} and Some(v) encodes {"some":v}; the null-sugar encoding and any other member shape are rejected, and any legal type may sit under an option.
Enums and variants are closed: unknown enum values and unknown variant cases are rejected (fail-closed).
An AFIDL1 module declares afidl 1; any other language major is rejected.
Schema family identity is a strict SpecificationId: lowercase kebab namespace segments and a positive major without leading zeros.
The primitive universe is closed to the 13 registered builtin keywords; unknown lowercase identifiers in type position become named references and must resolve.
field_no is a positive u32; zero is rejected.
field_no values are unique within their record.
case_no is a positive u32; zero is rejected.
case_no values are unique within their variant.
value_no is a positive u32; zero is rejected.
value_no values are unique within their enum.
Source formatting, comments, declaration order and member source order are non-semantic: reordering never changes canonical bytes or digests.
Number and name bindings are semantic: changing a field_no, case_no, value_no or member name changes the TypeSchemaDigest.
Every named reference must resolve to a declared type in the compilation unit; unknown references are rejected.
Alias cycles, direct or indirect, are rejected.
Direct or indirect recursive named references - through record fields, variant cases, alias expansion or any list/map/option wrapper - are rejected (Phase 2A scoped restriction).
TypeSchemaDigest = SHA256("AF\0type-schema\0" || ACE1(canonical TypeSchema)), computed per named type.
An import names an exact SpecificationId, major included; version ranges (latest, ^1, >=1, 1.x, *), file paths, wildcards, re-exports and per-type alias imports do not exist in AFIDL1.

Import resolution uses an explicit, immutable, in-memory schema universe supplied by the caller: no registry lookup, no latest-version resolution, no filesystem read and no network access. An import of a specification absent from the universe is unknown_import_specification.
An import alias matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and is not a reserved keyword; aliases are unique within the module.
A module holds at most one alias per imported specification family, so one specification has exactly one source spelling.
Importing the module's own schema id is rejected; local types are referenced unqualified.
Import declarations appear only between the schema declaration and the first type declaration; an import after a declaration is rejected.
A qualified reference names a named AFIDL declaration only: qualified primitives such as core.int64 are rejected, because builtin primitives are always spelled bare.

An external type is reachable only through <import-alias>.<TypeName>. An unqualified name never resolves to an imported type (no implicit import, no shadowing, no resolution-order dependence), and a qualified reference never falls back to a local reference.

Import declarations and import aliases do not enter the canonical TypeSchema record (schema/name/body); a qualified reference lowers to the imported specification's full logical identity. An alias rename, an import reordering or an unused import therefore leaves every canonical byte and every TypeSchemaDigest unchanged.

The global named-type dependency graph over a module set - through alias targets, record fields, variant payloads and every list/map/option wrapper - must be acyclic; imports never bypass the recursion restriction. The module import graph itself may contain cycles.

Two modules may import each other; only a type dependency between them is a cycle. Requiring an acyclic import graph would reject legal schemas, so the recursion restriction is stated over the type graph.
ComponentContract is a closed thirteen-field semantic body with exact imports and no arbitrary extension field.
Exact ComponentIdentity enters semantic identity while publication version and implementation metadata remain outside.
Only a validator-created checked body may be hashed with the existing component-contract HashV1 domain.
Public I/O ports use independent positive namespaces and exact nominal TypeSchemaRef pins.
The Failure row remains a separate exact-pinned proof dimension in the assembled contract.
Effect operations and exact resource types require explicit complete relation coverage.
Effect selectors bind only to declared resource ports and exact mapped resource attributes.
Information-flow sources and sinks resolve in their exact input, resource and output namespaces.
Usage ceilings remain exact additive declarations and missing recovery coordinates are not zero.
Recovery actions bind complete forward/action EffectAtom identities and form an acyclic dependency graph.
Execution constraints are resolved against explicit capability and profile universes.
Unknown provenance or influence never establishes an unjustified positive flow proof.
An effect selector requires a declared resource port, exact resource pin, full qualifier profile and closed operation support.
EffectFlowPartitions retain full atom identity and only narrow an existing operation-level flow ceiling.
Every required K action has exactly one exact ε binding and no undeclared action is accepted.
Recovery meter coverage is exhaustive and activation, attempt and usage bounds use checked arithmetic.
Any non-Proven required dimension prevents a Proven aggregate contract verdict.
F/X relations match exact labels, taints, authority levels, flow kinds, sinks, regions and trust domains.
Proof context pins canonical relation content and changed snapshots invalidate prior proof results.
Substitution uses exact I/O pins and existing directional dimension proofs; unsupported refinements remain Unproven.
Static compatibility and relation proofs never create runtime authority, worker attestation or execution authorization.

Each K action possibility must be contained by the exact declared action epsilon guard under frozen containment; a Violation requires a validator-created type-valid reachable countermodel, otherwise the relation remains Unproven, and no guard proof creates receipt eligibility.
HashV1(domain, payload) = SHA256("AF" || 0x00 || domain || 0x00 || payload); the prefix is the exact ASCII bytes AF + NUL.
The two NUL separators frame the domain byte-exactly, so payloads containing AF, NUL or full preimages can never be reinterpreted.
SHA-256 is the only HashV1 algorithm in v1; other algorithms are rejected.
A DigestRef retains its domain for its whole life; digests never degrade to bare hex strings.
DigestRef hex is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; uppercase hex, wrong lengths and non-hex characters are rejected.
The HashV1 domain set is closed and centrally registered; unknown domains are rejected and adding a domain is an explicit registry addition.
For a fixed payload, hashing under two different registry domains yields different digests; the invariant holds over the whole registry.

An effect signature is a static declaration, never authorization: Declared != Granted != Dispatched != Observed, Dispatched ⊆ Granted ⊆ Declared is a Runtime/Effect-Gateway invariant, and no API converts a signature into authority.
An effect atom is exactly operation + resource selector + closed qualifiers; canonical identity includes qualifier family, member discriminant and semantic payload, never family alone.
An operation identity is catalog (a SpecificationId) plus a dotted lowercase name; resolution against the supplied explicit catalog universe is fail-closed with no default catalog and no fallback.

A resource selector is a >= 1 requirement port plus exact-binding scope constraints; it never carries a raw handle, filesystem root, database connection, secret or worker endpoint, and scope containment is exact-binding set inclusion, never a prefix match.

Occurrence bounds are explicit [lower, upper] intervals with an explicit unbounded ceiling (never UINT64_MAX); they count logical effect occurrences, physical attempts are tracked separately, and impossible intervals are rejected.
Pure is exactly the closed empty row; zero-occurrence entries are semantically pure and dropped by the canonical form.
The unknown row (⊤) is an unprovable-envelope analysis result: it is not pure, contaminates compositions upward, carries no capability material and is never authorization.
A bounded-open row keeps known effects plus a residual ceiling that must constrain something (a scope binding or a finite occurrence upper); an open row that bounds nothing is pure.

Containment (⊑) must be PROVED per entry (exact operation, equal qualifiers, narrower scope, contained interval, implied guard) or returned as NOT PROVEN with a stable reason; unresolved proofs fail closed as effect_envelope_unprovable.

Accumulation (⊕) adds occurrence intervals per atom key with checked arithmetic, keeps distinct atoms, composes guards conservatively (lower bounds only across unconditional entries), and is the identity of the pure row.

Branch join (⊔) keeps the possible effects of both mutually exclusive branches: a guarded lower bound is guaranteed only under its guard — identical guards keep the conditional minimum, different conditions widen to unconditional with the lower bound weakened to zero, and one-sided keys drop to [0, u] with their guard kept.
RACE is conservative accumulation over ALL contestants: a loser may have produced effects before cancellation, so loser effects are never discarded and race is not a branch join.
ITERATE scales the body envelope by the statically proven repetition bounds; an unprovable repetition count never yields a finite envelope, and zero repetitions are pure.

RETRY separates physical attempt bounds [1, max_attempts] from the logical effect envelope, which stays conservatively scaled (no idempotency assumption) and records the explicit obligation that narrowing requires a recovery contract.
Compensation adds the counter-effect to the envelope and never subtracts forward effects: the original effect and the counter-effect are both facts.

Canonicalization is deterministic and idempotent: entry order, scope binding order and qualifier order never change the canonical ACE1 bytes; declared duplicates are rejected (not merged); and no EffectSignatureDigest or new HashV1 domain is introduced.

The guard language is closed (unconditional, typed input equality): guards narrow when an effect may occur, their grammar is validated, and inexpressible conditions widen to unconditional instead of being assumed false.
Occurrence arithmetic is checked: overflow is the explicit error effect_arithmetic_overflow, never a wrap-around and never a silent saturation into a smaller envelope.

Execution Requirements is a static declaration/proof layer only: it contains no worker identity, endpoint, lease, credential, heartbeat, live load, live price, reservation, scheduler state, placement result or HashV1 digest.
Hard constraints are conjunctive eligibility conditions; closed soft preferences never compensate for a hard rejection or unproven fact.
Capability matching uses the complete explicit catalog/name identity and an explicitly recognized exact version; unknown capability or version fails closed.
Capability attributes are NFC-normalized, non-empty, sorted and checked against the explicit vocabulary; unknown attributes are not silently compatible.
CPU millicores, memory bytes and GPU device count are independent unsigned units; quantity capacity is nominal, checked only within a unit, and missing evidence is unproven rather than zero.
Sandbox assurance is a closed basic/strong hard requirement; a weak descriptor rejects and an absent descriptor is unproven, while the level is not enforcement or attestation.
Trust domains are exact nominal identities resolved from an explicit universe; matching never infers provider, parent, identity, delegation or authority equivalence.
Execution region and data residency are separate hard constraints; nominal region identities require explicit resolution and never use prefix, geography or provider inference.
Runtime profile and implementation ABI requirements use exact explicit identity/feature/digest pins; missing or incompatible evidence is not implicitly compatible.
Canonicalization resolves explicit universes, rejects duplicate hard requirements, sorts unordered dimensions deterministically and is idempotent; no requirement is silently relaxed.
Static profile matching checks every hard constraint conjunctively and returns only descriptor proof, rejection or unproven evidence; it is not availability, admission or placement.
Feasibility compares old eligible profiles as a subset of new eligible profiles; added requirements or narrowed regions are not deployment compatible by default.
A feasibility expansion does not prove security preservation; sandbox, trust and residency relaxation is independently reported as a security violation or unproven relation.
Combined compatibility requires both independent feasibility and security verdicts and never hides their directions in one boolean.
X does not create execution authority and does not blindly aggregate control-tree requirements into a fictitious worker or scheduler surface; cross-dimension composition is deferred.

A failure type is nominal: the full (SpecificationId, TypeName, pinned TypeSchemaDigest) triple; the same short name under a different specification or with a different digest is a DIFFERENT failure type, never silently compatible.
The Failure Row is a closed set of nominal types with no open/residual/unknown wire state; unknown upper bounds are the analysis-level Unproven result, never a row variant.
Every payload pin resolves exactly against the explicit schema universe: the type must exist and the pinned digest must match; there is no latest-schema fallback.
The empty row is the algebra identity but does NOT mean the computation succeeds: TimedOut, Cancelled, RecoveryBlocked, TaskAttemptLost and RuntimeIncident all remain possible outside the row.
An unprovable failure upper bound is Unproven and demanding a row from it fails closed (failure_row_unproven); unknown is never interpreted as the empty row.
Canonical ordering is deterministic: refs sorted by full nominal identity in byte order; declaration order and map iteration order never reach the canonical ACE1 bytes.
Duplicate declarations of the same nominal type are rejected; the algebra's union may deduplicate - declaration and algebra are deliberately separate.
Containment is exact nominal membership: never inferred from the same short name, a similar schema or equal record fields; a future compatibility system needs an explicit proof.
Union is commutative, associative and idempotent with the empty row as identity; branch composition (SELECT/PARALLEL/RACE) is exactly set union.

A handled failure type must be declared by the child row: a HANDLE matcher matches an exact TypeSchemaRef the child declares, and a handled-but-undeclared type is rejected (failure_not_declared), never pretended matched.
Unhandled failures propagate verbatim: the residual computation keeps every declared type not handled.
Handler failures propagate: handlers may fail themselves and their rows union into the result ((child minus H) union handlers), never treated as automatically handled.
TimedOut is a Control Outcome (the frozen HandleMatch::timed_out), never a failure type; TIMEOUT composition adds no type to the child row.
Cancelled is a Control Outcome: parent cancellation is never a normal failure, no cancelled matcher exists, and no cancellation failure type can be introduced.
RecoveryBlocked is a Recovery State: not a Workflow failure, not catchable by an ordinary HANDLE, never mapped into a business failure type by retry or compensation logic.

TaskAttemptLost is an Infrastructure Fact (never automatically Failure<WorkerLost>) and RuntimeIncident lives on the Incident Plane; operational conditions and platform degradation are likewise outside the Failure Row.
RETRY preserves the child's failure row verbatim: retry attempts are not a proof that business failure is impossible, and only a future Recovery/Replay Contract may narrow it.
Provenance, Trust, Taint and Information Flow stay four distinct concepts: no trust score, no single trusted flag, and no collapse of the influence dimensions into one value.

Label identity is nominal (catalog SpecificationId, label name) resolved by the explicit read-only universe: unknown catalog or label rejected, duplicates rejected, no auto-registration, no case-insensitive matching, and label order never enters semantic identity.
Confidentiality restrictions and taints are structurally separate nominal types: where data may go and what may have influenced a value are never unified into one collection.
No confidentiality hierarchy is invented: containment is set membership plus explicit catalog rules; no total order over user-defined labels exists from which downgrade flows could be claimed.

Ordinary data transformation MUST NOT elevate instruction authority: content claiming to be a system instruction stays external_data, source authentication is not instruction authorization, and a MAX authority is only a may-carry upper bound, never effective instruction authority or endorsement.

Taint propagation is may-influence conservative: the output taint is the union over all inputs that MAY influence it; an incomplete influence relation yields the explicit unknown or the conservative union of all possible inputs, and no author can prove a real influence away with an incomplete list.

The LLM strong taint mixer: all model-visible inputs may influence all model outputs, so output taint is the union of every visible input taint plus model_generated, influence stays unknown, and authority is never elevated.
A model output is never endorsed: model said verified does not become endorsed, and summarizing untrusted web does not become trusted knowledge.
Data egress and decision influence are separate flow kinds, checked separately and never compared across: no data leak does not imply no decision influence, and vice versa.

External-effect sinks reuse the structured EffectOperationRef by exact cross-module identity and resolve fail-closed against the explicit catalog; classification comes only from the catalog, never from the operation name, and referencing an effect is not being granted it.
An unclassifiable sink yields Unproven, never an assumption of safety; sink-port 0 is rejected.

A declared flow ceiling is not an observed flow and not a policy approval: every judgment is ProvenWithinDeclaredCeiling, RequiresTrustedTransformation (an obligation, not an event) or Unproven - never an authorization.

Declassification and endorsement are separate privileged transformations; ordinary tasks cannot self-declare either, and this phase records at most the obligations requires_declassification / requires_endorsement.

No static transformation without an authorization proof deletes a taint or lowers a confidentiality restriction: the wire model expresses no such operation and this phase executes no declassifier or endorser.
Persistence does not imply trust: store, load, serialize, deserialize and summarize round-trips return data with its original taints and provenance influence.

The five unknowns are distinct and never collapsed to an empty list: unknown source is the explicit unknown_external category, unknown influence is the sticky influence_unknown Top, unknown labels and sinks are validation errors, and canonicalization never repairs unknown into a lower-risk state; an explicit unknown_external source is never sufficient for a positive flow proof even when the summary claims clean influence.

Flow non-relaxation: F_new must not relax F_old - per kind the new ceiling set must be a subset of the old, confidentiality restrictions a superset, authority not elevated, taint and source capacity not narrowed, unknown influence not repaired; undecidable containment is Unproven and never a substitution approval.

Canonical flow form is deterministic: resolved nominal label identities, sets sorted by identity bytes (constraints by kind and sink coordinate), duplicates rejected, declaration order never reaching the canonical ACE1 bytes.
Recovery Contract is a static declaration and proof layer only: it does not create receipts, grants, keys, runtime state or execution.
ReplaySemantics is closed at recompute, recorded, reconcile and forbidden with distinct static obligations.
Replay declaration is not authority, safe retry permission, runtime evidence or historical/fork equivalence.
IdempotencySemantics is closed at natural, keyed, none and reconciled; each is a declaration rather than provider proof.
KEYED recovery carries explicit key stability obligations and never generates an IdempotencyKey or durable Invocation/Attempt identity.

Effect recovery clauses use the complete canonical EffectAtom identity including the full selector and qualifier family, member discriminant and semantic payload; family alone cannot match and duplicates reject.
Every known recoverable Effect requires an explicit matching clause; unknown/open effect coverage is not assumed safe.
Reconciliation requirement declares capability/evidence obligations; it never creates APPLIED, NOT_APPLIED, PARTIALLY_APPLIED or STILL_UNKNOWN runtime evidence.
Unknown effects may only block or require reconciliation; UNKNOWN is never blindly retried and PARTIALLY_APPLIED is never coerced to another result.
Compensation is a new explicit Effect operation obligation, not an execution grant, rollback API or hidden method.
Compensation preserves forward Effect history and never subtracts forward Usage/Cost or erases Failure/Cancelled/Timeout facts.
Static safety returns ProvenStaticConstraint, RequiresEvidence, Unproven or Violation; Proven is never runtime retry authorization.
Recovery compatibility is conservative: exact-equivalent declarations are proven, removed capability is weakened and other mode changes are Unproven; enum order is not a strength order.
K-to-ε/Φ/U correspondence is explicit future integration; RecoveryBlocked is not a business FailureValue and no temporary ComponentContract exists.
Recovery adds no Receipt, Grant, Reconciliation execution, Compensation execution, journal, runtime, scheduler, worker or Recovery digest/domain.
RuleId syntax is AF-<AREA>-<4DIGIT> with the area from the closed rule-area table and number 0001..9999; ids derived from document section numbering are forbidden.
RuleIds are unique and are never reused for a different normative meaning.

Every rule's source_anchor exists in its normative source (Markdown anchor or heading slug, or an AFIDL type name); two rules never bind the same (path, anchor) pair; line numbers are forbidden as anchors.
Every conformance reference resolves to an existing fixture case id, file-based case id or declared suite id.
A retired ABI number is never reassigned to a different symbolic meaning, and a symbolic name never moves to a different number, within its (schema_family, type_name, number_kind) scope.

Every AFIDL module under spec/idl matches the ABI registry for its family: all current bindings have active rows with identical names, all active rows have schema counterparts, retired and reserved numbers are unused.
(schema_family, type_name, number_kind, number) is unique and a symbolic name is unique within its scope; identifiers follow the AFIDL grammars and numbers are positive.
Registry JSON files are deterministically formatted (2-space indent, LF, final newline, lexicographically sorted keys) and their arrays follow the frozen canonical orders.

A ResourceTypeRef is exact-pinned: nominal identity is the full (SpecificationId, TypeName, pinned TypeSchemaDigest) triple; an unregistered schema or a wrong digest is rejected, the same short name is never accepted.

A resource type must be explicitly recognized by the explicit, read-only ResourceTypeUniverse: a legal AFIDL schema alone is not a resource type, and recognition pins the type's closed attribute vocabulary.
A resource requirement does not grant authority: requirement satisfaction is a static predicate, never an authorization, and no requirement-satisfied-implies-grant path exists.
A requirement port must be positive (port_no > 0); port 0 is rejected.
Resource ports must be unique within one requirement row: one contract interface declares at most one requirement per port.
Requirement attributes are canonical: NFC-normalized text, unsigned UTF-8 key order, and the same semantic requirements always produce the same canonical ACE1 bytes.
Duplicate normalized attribute keys are rejected: two different values for one key are never silently overwritten, and NFC-equivalent spellings are the same key, not a legal equivalence input.
The requirement row is a closed set with no open/residual/unknown wire state; canonical order is ascending port number.
An unknown requirement upper bound is never the empty row: empty would falsely claim the computation needs nothing.
There is no implicit latest lookup: resolution is exact against the explicitly supplied universe, with no fallback and no implicit upcast.
Static satisfaction requires the exact resource type: same short name, same record shape or similar provider is never accepted, and satisfaction proves nothing beyond static attribute matching.

A requirement row cannot be strengthened: within one port namespace the new row's accepted candidate set must contain the old row's (per retained port, new.required_attributes subset of old.required_attributes as full (key,value) pairs); a new port or a new/changed condition proves strengthening.
No implicit ResourceType subtyping exists: a retained port with a changed nominal type (including the same short name under a different pin) is Unproven, never compatible.

Resource ports are local to one contract interface: comparing rows of two different namespaces is not a static proof and fails closed; equal port numbers across components do not name the same resource.
No cross-component merge without an explicit port mapping: aggregating requirement rows by equal port numbers is forbidden and no merge operation exists in this layer.
The ResourceHandle capability ceiling, EffectGrant and ResourceRequirement are distinct: declaring a requirement produces no runtime authority and no attenuation.

Attribute constraints form a closed exact-value conjunctive predicate language: an attribute key outside the type's descriptor vocabulary has no known constraint meaning and is rejected; no glob, regex, path prefix, CIDR, policy expression or predicate script exists.
Unproven is a fail-closed analysis result: it never enters the wire model, is never interpreted as the empty row and is never auto-judged compatible.
The workflow semantic primitive universe is closed to the nine registered primitives with value_no 1..9; no other type may enter the workflow value layer.
int32, uint32, uint64 and float64 are machine-only and MUST NOT surface as workflow value types at any point.

Composite workflow types are expressed as a document-local indexed type DAG whose list/map_string/option cases reference other nodes by SemanticTypeId; recursive AFIDL schemas are neither required nor permitted.
Semantic type ids are positive and unique within the document; the canonical type table is ordered by id ascending and source order never affects identity.
The semantic type DAG MUST be acyclic: a type that expands through itself, directly or transitively, is rejected.
A TypeSchemaRef pins <SpecificationId>/<TypeName> together with the exact TypeSchemaDigest it was authored against; a published reference is never re-resolved against a later schema of that name.

A TypeSchemaRef is valid only when the identity resolves in the supplied TypeSchemaUniverse and the pinned digest equals that schema's actual canonical digest; a merely well-formed digest is not sufficient.

A digest reference is the DigestRefValue record (algorithm/domain/hex); algorithm is sha256, the domain is a member of the frozen HashV1 registry (type-schema for a TypeSchemaRef) and hex is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. A bare digest string is forbidden.

A value slot is an immutable SSA binding: one producer and zero-or-more consumers, with no mutation operation. Phase 3A validates slot identity and type only; producer consistency belongs to the semantic IR dataflow stage.
Local ids in every namespace are > 0 and unique within the document; 0 is reserved as invalid/unset and no further reserved ranges exist.

SemanticTypeId, ValueSlotId, ExpressionId and ResourceSlotId are four independent namespaces: identical numbers in two namespaces denote unrelated objects, and a value never travels through a resource slot.
PrimitiveConstant is closed to the nine workflow primitives and its cases map 1:1 onto SemanticPrimitiveType; bytes payloads are canonical unpadded base64url.
Expressions are pure and deterministic: no I/O, no clock, no randomness, no environment, no policy or registry query and no resource access; they never produce effects.
The expression body set is closed to the fifteen registered expressions; arithmetic, string operators, indexing, variant inspection and every fallible operation are absent.
Expressions form a DAG: forward references are legal and cycles (self, two-node or longer) are rejected.
Every expression, value slot and semantic type reference must resolve; unresolved references are rejected.
The validator implements a real type checker: every expression derives its result type from its body and the declared result_type must equal the derived type.
Record construction and field_get select fields by field_no; variant construction and enum selection use case_no and value_no. Numbers are the durable schema ABI, names remain value-encoding keys.
Map construction applies the ACE1 key invariants during validation: keys are NFC-normalized, keys colliding after normalization are rejected, and entries are stored in unsigned UTF-8 byte order.
A resource slot is a logical requirement declaration in its own namespace: values never travel through resource slots and a ResourceSlotId is unrelated to a ValueSlotId with the same number.
A resource slot's definition is immutable for the life of the document and its requirement_type pins an exact contract schema.
No ResourceHandle, binding snapshot or runtime resource object exists at the semantic layer; a resource slot is a logical requirement only.
Type nodes, value slots, expressions and resource slots are canonically ordered by id ascending; source order never enters identity.
Phase 3A introduces no new HashV1 domain: type identity comes from TypeSchemaDigest and the semantic objects are ordinary ACE1 objects.

The Semantic IR is a static model: validation, canonicalization and the document digest only. No interpreter, plan, worker, region, endpoint, credential, lease or scheduler placement exists in this layer.
No opcode state machine, runtime command or journal event exists at the IR layer; runtime semantics belong to the later execution stages.
Runtime occurrence identity (OccurrencePath, AttemptId, InvocationId) does not exist in the IR: a loop or retry holds one static body definition, never per-occurrence copies.
CallComposite is authoring/compiler-only and MUST NOT appear in canonical IR; the construct is lowered before this layer.
Trigger is not a computation: it belongs to deployment binding and has no opcode and no node in the IR.
SemanticIrDocument carries the reused Phase 3A tables plus semantic_refs, contracts, run_parameters, workflow_outputs, computations and root, with the frozen field numbering.
A semantic ref pins an exact canonical SpecificationId: syntax is validated, references are unique and canonically ordered; registry knownness belongs to compiler tooling, never to af-ir.

The types/values/expressions/resources tables reuse agentflow.semantic.core@1 objects by identity via the AFIDL import; redeclaring copies is forbidden, and the tables must pass the Phase 3A validation.

Canonical ordering is frozen for every table and nested list: identity tables by id, semantic_refs by canonical SpecificationId bytes, workflow_outputs by NFC name bytes, ports and ordinals ascending.

ComputationId, RunParameterId and ContractRefId are independent id namespaces and PortNo, BranchOrdinal and HandlerOrdinal are numbering spaces; all are u32 newtypes, values are > 0 and 0 is rejected by validation.

Every declared value slot has exactly one producer: 0 producers is unbound_value_slot and more than one is duplicate_value_producer. Producers are run parameters, computation outputs, iterate item slots and iterate carry slots.
An expression is pure derived computation and is never a value-slot producer; expression ids do not materialize slots.
A run parameter produces its value slot: parameter.type must equal the slot's type and no other producer may bind the same slot.
A run parameter name is non-empty, NFC-normalized and unique after NFC; names may be any Unicode and canonical order is by RunParameterId, never by name.
RunParameterDecl is a static workflow input declaration only: no default value, admission snapshot, mutable parameter, runtime update, constraint or secret flag exists in this layer.

A workflow output is a name plus an expression; the output type is the expression's result_type and is never duplicated. Output names follow the run-parameter name rules with canonical order by NFC name bytes.
ContractRefKind is closed at exactly component (1) and subflow (2); entries are canonically ordered by ContractRefId and duplicate ids are rejected.
A component contract reference pins sha256 over the frozen component-contract domain; any other domain is rejected.
A subflow contract reference pins sha256 over the frozen semantic-ir domain: CALL_SUBFLOW references an exact published Semantic IR identity. No workflow-contract or subflow-contract domain exists.
One exact contract identity (algorithm, domain, hex) has at most one table entry per document; digest validation covers shape and domain only - there is no Contract Store in this layer.
A computation's output ports are positive and unique, bound to declared value slots; the port's type is the slot's type and is never stored twice.

The ownership edge set is exactly the per-opcode child table (INVOKE/AWAIT/CALL_SUBFLOW: 0 local children; SEQUENCE: N; SELECT: N cases; PARALLEL/RACE: N branches; ITERATE/RETRY/TIMEOUT/SCOPE/COMPENSATION_SCOPE: 1; HANDLE: 1 protected child + N handlers); every child reference must resolve.

The computations form a structured ownership tree: the root exists and has no parent, every non-root computation has exactly one parent, nothing is detached, and neither cycles nor unreachable computations exist.
Dataflow edges (expression reads a value slot) and ownership edges (a computation owns a child) are different relations handled by different validator logic; no universal Edge type exists.
ComputationInterface is a read-only projection port_no -> SemanticTypeId derived from outputs and slot types; no second interface table may be stored anywhere.

Wrapper interface equality is static: SEQUENCE equals its last child, SELECT every case, RACE every branch, RETRY/TIMEOUT/SCOPE/COMPENSATION_SCOPE the child, HANDLE the protected child plus every handler; PARALLEL is checked by its explicit output mapping and ITERATE by the carry rules.
INVOKE, AWAIT and CALL_SUBFLOW are leaves: their output interface is declared only by their own outputs; contract-level checking is deferred.

The SEQUENCE child list order is the semantic execution order: it is preserved verbatim and never canonically re-sorted; a sequence has at least one child and its output interface equals the last child's.

The SELECT selector has type int64 and produces the exact case ordinal to run: no truthiness, no source-order matching, no fall-through. Ordinals are positive, unique and canonically ascending; a select has at least one case.
All SELECT case children share the parent's output interface: the typed merge shell is checked statically; runtime case selection is not part of this phase.
ParallelMode is closed at all (1) and fail_fast (2); a parallel has at least one branch with positive unique ordinals in canonical ascending order.

The explicit parallel output mapping is the only path from branch outputs into the parent interface: parent ports are unique across bindings, branch and child ports must exist, and the parent slot's type equals the child output slot's type.
max_inflight is a semantic concurrency bound: option<uint32> with Some(0) invalid. Worker count, tenant quota, region capacity and scheduler limits are physical concerns and MUST NOT enter the IR.
A race has at least two branches with positive unique ordinals and one shared output interface; v1 semantics is exactly FIRST_TERMINAL with no winner_policy knob.
FOREACH: the source expression has type list<T>, the item slot exists with type T and its producer is this ITERATE; max_inflight follows the parallel bound rules.
WHILE: the guard has type bool and max_iterations > 0 - v1 has no unbounded while. The guard may reference carry slots; availability and dominance analysis is Phase 3C.

A loop carry binding requires the slot to exist, the initial expression to exist, the body output port to exist, and slot.type == initial.result_type == body-output-slot.type; one binding per carry slot. Loops never mutate: values are new occurrences.

RETRY carries an explicit finite delay schedule: maximum occurrence count is exactly 1 + len(delays); delays are durations >= 0 and their order is semantic (never sorted); no wall clock, jitter or runtime policy lookup exists.
TIMEOUT bounds one child by a duration-valued expression; there is no TimerId, TimerState or TimerCommand. AWAIT has no built-in timeout: compose TIMEOUT(AWAIT(...)).

HandleMatch is closed at failure (exact typed TypeSchemaRef match) and timed_out (unit); there is no cancelled case. Handler ordinals are positive and unique; failure clauses are pairwise disjoint by exact schema; at most one timed_out clause exists.

A scope lists the logical resources it statically owns/allows: they must exist, be unique, and are canonically ascending. Only the ownership and lexical boundaries are frozen - authority/budget attenuation, deadline and cancellation state and ResourceHandle are later, separately specified tables.

COMPENSATION_SCOPE owns one child and holds no compensation task list; compensation sources are later derived from committed effect receipts plus effect compensation contracts, and a COMPENSATION_SCOPE MUST NOT erase forward computation or effect history.

SemanticIrDigest = HashV1("semantic-ir", ACE1(CanonicalSemanticIrDocument)); the domain is the Phase 1 frozen registry entry, no new domain is introduced, and the digest is computed over the canonical form only.

INVOKE calls an exact component contract with semantic inputs and resource requirements; input and resource ports are positive and unique and their expressions/resources must exist. No TaskDefinition, Binding, Invocation, Attempt or Worker exists at this layer.
AWAIT is a passive durable wait with an exact digest-pinned signal_type and a correlation expression; no mailbox, timer, webhook or approval state exists in this layer.
CALL_SUBFLOW references a subflow-kind contract (an exact published Semantic IR digest), has zero local children and no detach/fire-and-forget: the subflow is an owned durable child boundary.
Exactly two lists carry semantic order and are never canonically re-sorted: SEQUENCE children (execution order) and RETRY delays (schedule order); changing their order changes the SemanticIrDigest.

A value slot may be read at a use site only if its single producer dominates that use site in the structured ownership tree: slot existence (Phase 3B) is not availability, and the analysis adds value_not_available without touching any Phase 3B error kind.
Run parameters are available from the root entry, in every descendant computation under every control branch, for the whole run: they are the immutable workflow inputs.

A computation's outputs become available only after that computation's structured completion boundary: an output MUST NOT be used at its own entry, a parent output MUST NOT be used inside its own subtree, and a timeout duration is evaluated at the timeout entry.

Only a computation's own declared outputs cross its ownership boundary: a raw child, grandchild, case, branch, handler or loop-body output consumed outside its owner is rejected as outside_owner_boundary.
SEQUENCE is the only multi-child control form whose child order is dataflow: each child's entry environment is the sequence entry plus every earlier direct sibling's own exports, cumulatively.
A SEQUENCE child MUST NOT read a later sibling's export: future reference is use-before-producer and is rejected.

SELECT cases are mutually isolated and start from the select's entry environment: the selector evaluates before any case, case ordinals are identity keys (never execution order), and one case MUST NOT read another case's output.
PARALLEL branches are mutually isolated: every branch starts from the parallel's entry environment and no branch may consume another branch's output, in any completion mode.
RACE branches are mutually isolated: FIRST_TERMINAL gives no stable branch order, so no branch may consume another branch's output and no raw branch output (winner or loser) escapes the race.

HANDLE clauses are mutually isolated and see exactly the handle's entry environment: a handler MUST NOT read the protected child's outputs (it runs precisely when those outputs may not exist) and no FailureValue or failure-slot placeholder is created.
A foreach source is a pre-loop snapshot expression: it evaluates once from the iterate's entry environment and MUST NOT reference the item slot, a carry slot or a body output.

Every loop-carry initial evaluates from the same pre-loop environment: no initial may read the item slot or any carry slot, so the canonical carry order (by slot id) never becomes an evaluation order.
A foreach body sees the iterate's entry environment plus the item slot and every carry slot.
A while guard and body see the iterate's entry environment plus every carry slot; the guard evaluates at the loop header and never reads a body computation output directly.
Loop-local values cannot escape their iterate: a foreach item slot, a carry slot and a loop-body output MUST NOT be read outside the iterate computation; outside it only Iterate.outputs are visible.

Only the root computation's own outputs and the immutable run parameters are visible to workflow-output expressions: WorkflowExitValues = RunParameterSlots + Exports(root); a raw root-descendant output is rejected.
Expression availability is checked per use site and never cached per expression: the same ExpressionDef may be legal inside its owning branch and illegal at a use site outside it.
An expression referenced by no use site creates no execution and never fails availability: an expression definition is not an execution.

A SCOPE narrows resource visibility: its listed set MUST be a subset of the inherited environment and its child sees exactly the listed set (never the union); an omitted resource is resource_not_visible inside the scope.
A nested SCOPE cannot widen resources: it cannot reintroduce a resource its parent scope omitted.
InvokeBody.resources and CallSubflowBody.resources are the resource use sites: every used slot MUST be lexically visible at the computation's entry environment.

EntryResources(root) is every declared resource slot; every opcode but SCOPE inherits its parent's environment unchanged, narrowing ends at the scope boundary, and visibility is shared not owned: parallel branches may use the same visible resource and no resource_shared_in_parallel error exists.

The Phase 3C analysis is derived-only: SemanticDataflowAnalysis is never ACE1-encoded, never hashed into the SemanticIrDigest, and absent from AFIDL, the ABI registry and the wire model; it runs strictly after Phase 3B validation so old error kinds never move.

Phase 3C freezes the durable surfaces: semantic-ir.afidl stays byte-identical (36 TypeSchemaDigests), the 13 ComputationBody cases stay frozen, and no AFIDL module, ABI row, HashV1 domain or Rule Area is added.

A CALL_SUBFLOW target resolves only by its exact pinned SemanticIrDigest in an explicit, immutable, in-memory universe whose keys are full DigestRefs (sha256 / semantic-ir / hex); the digest is always computed from the target document itself.
A missing target digest fails closed: there is no same-name latest fallback, no filesystem, registry, network, package or deployment lookup anywhere in the subflow universe.

The subflow interface is a derived static view of the target's own run_parameters, workflow_outputs and resources tables: it never enters AFIDL, the ABI registry or the SemanticIrDigest, and no SemanticTypeDigest or interface digest exists.
Input ports enumerate the target run parameters in RunParameterId canonical order, 1-based; source table order never matters.
Output ports enumerate the target workflow outputs in canonical NFC-name byte order, 1-based; source table order never matters.
Every declared target ResourceSlot is part of the resource requirement interface (not only the currently used ones); resource ports enumerate the slots in ResourceSlotId canonical order, 1-based.

Subflow interface port ordinals are derived external interface coordinates, not aliases for RunParameterId, workflow-output names or ResourceSlotId; the three port namespaces are independent and target names are diagnostic metadata only.

Cross-document types compare structurally, never by local SemanticTypeId: primitives compare by keyword and containers recursively, so the same structure under different local ids is compatible and the same id with different meanings is not.
A schema leaf compares the exact complete TypeSchemaRef - specification_id, type_name and schema_digest; the same record name under a different specification version is a different type.
CALL_SUBFLOW inputs must exactly match the target input interface: the bound port set equals 1..N (no missing, no extra port) and every bound expression's resolved type equals the target port type.

CALL_SUBFLOW outputs must exactly match the target output interface: the declared port set equals 1..N and every declared slot's resolved type equals the target port type; an unconsumed output stays an unused slot, never a partial contract.

CALL_SUBFLOW resources must exactly match the target resource interface: the bound port set equals 1..N and every bound slot's requirement_type equals the target requirement_type as an exact TypeSchemaRef.

A fixed SemanticIrDigest implies a fixed derived interface: table order moves neither the digest nor the interface, local type renumbering moves neither the interface shape, and a changed target always means a new digest that old callers never follow silently.
Subflow checking runs strictly after Phase 3B validation and the Phase 3C analysis, never changes their error kinds, and a document without CALL_SUBFLOW passes against an empty universe.

Interface derivation does not validate the target's transitive subflow closure, and subflow-graph cycles are not judged here: dependency closure and graph acyclicity belong to the later Resolver / LockGraph stage.
A component target resolves only by the complete exact digest pin in an explicit snapshot; identity comes from the checked contract, with no latest or name-only fallback.
INVOKE requires a digest-recomputed CheckedComponentContract under the exact snapshot proof-context object; unresolved targets are never pure.
Component input/output mappings require exact port numbers, exact public TypeSchemaRef pins, and existing Phase 3C scope, dominance, and producer proofs; local types are not public type evidence.
Component resource ports map explicitly to visible ResourceSlotIds with exact resource type pins; absent attribute evidence remains Unproven and aliases never reduce bounds or grant authority.
Scoped effects retain exact source contract, full atom qualifiers, bounds, caller digest and node identity; distinct call sites never merge by contract digest.
Flow coordinates map only through exact I/O/R/effect mappings; unknown origins, influence, taints and authority bounds remain conservative and are never dropped or elevated.
Checked Failure/Effect/Flow/Usage/Recovery/Execution declarations remain per-invocation summaries; missing dimensions are not empty, and this phase performs no scaling or workflow placement closure.
CALL_SUBFLOW resolves its exact SemanticIrDigest in the Phase 3D universe and reuses the Phase 3D call-site interface checker.
A subflow export requires a complete checked ComponentContract whose exact I/O/R pins match the derived target interface; derived I/O/R never synthesizes missing dimensions.
Resolving a subflow export declaration does not prove body conformance; absent a trusted complete proof the relation remains RequiresEvidence.
The explicit exact-digest dependency closure fails closed on cycles and reports missing targets as Unproven without recursive expansion.
AWAIT preserves its exact signal pin and correlation while missing adapter dimensions remain partial; it has no implicit timeout, Effect dispatch, business cancellation failure, or authority uplift.
ComponentContractDigest depends on canonical semantic body, not proof context; checked positive claims remain context-bound and must be revalidated after context change.
A control result is a source-traceable non-wire DerivedControlContractSummary, never a CheckedComponentContract or digest input.
Bottom-up traversal requires the exact current caller SemanticIrDigest, proof-context object, validator-created leaf summaries and Phase 3C evidence.

Unknown or unsupported control operators remain Unproven; known descendants are not discarded and no row defaults empty. The formerly unsupported SCOPE and COMPENSATION_SCOPE now use the additive Phase 4B.2B.3 rules.
SEQUENCE preserves semantic child order, uses existing Effect accumulation, weakens later-child lower bounds when prior success is not proven, and retains upper bounds/occurrences.
SELECT uses the frozen exclusive Effect branch_join and Usage maximum, retaining complete AtomKey qualifiers and guard-sensitive lower bounds.
SELECT totality is not invented without a default/range proof; selector dependencies remain decision influence and cannot elevate authority.
The frozen PARALLEL all mode accumulates every branch's possible Effect and Usage; max_inflight is concurrency only, and outputs use the explicit typed branch mapping.
PARALLEL fail_fast retains sibling Effect/Usage/Failure facts despite cancellation and weakens lower bounds whose full execution is not guaranteed.
RACE is FIRST_TERMINAL, not a SELECT join: all contestants including losers contribute Effect and Usage upper bounds, with only unguaranteed lower bounds weakened.
RACE retains every contestant's exact Recovery/K and per-action Usage source facts, including losers; compensation never subtracts forward effects.
Failure rows union across possible branches; cancellation/timeout are not typed business Failure, and static analysis never selects a physical winner or primary cause.
Control outputs reuse checked IR interfaces, Phase 3C producer evidence and explicit Parallel branch/port mapping; local types are not public schema aliases.
Flow sources/taints union conservatively, may-carry authority takes its existing upper bound, unknown remains sticky, and selector/sequence/winner influence is not discarded.
Usage uses checked accumulation or exclusive join by (phase,meter); missing coordinates remain Unknown, Forward/Recovery stay separate, and no retry/concurrency multiplier is inferred.
Recovery contracts, action identities and profiles remain per child; RACE losers do not lose declared recovery obligations.
Resource ports stay source-scoped; numeric port equality never merges namespaces, and aliases require the exact same caller ResourceSlotId.
ExecutionRequirements remain per child and are not summed into a single Worker, placement, admission or capacity requirement.
Repeated uses of one contract remain distinct by caller digest, control/leaf node, contract digest and source ordinal even if the envelope algebra combines equal AtomKeys.
Child Violation/Unproven/RequiresEvidence facts remain per-dimension obligations; a computed envelope cannot downgrade child evidence or be issued as a checked ComponentContract.
ITERATE uses conservative bounded repetition; dynamic FOREACH has no proven total count, max_inflight is not total work, and carry outputs require exact checked mapping.
RETRY preserves ordered finite delays and separate physical-attempt bounds, conservatively amplifies logical Effect/Usage, and evaluates existing K without runtime evidence or inferred retry policy.
TIMEOUT preserves child contracts and represents child completion and TimedOut separately; timeout never proves successful cancellation or zero incurred Effect/Usage.
HANDLE matches exact Failure schema pins, preserves unmatched residual failures, keeps TimedOut outside Phi, and composes handler Effect/Usage as conditional alternatives.
SCOPE compares exact Phase 3C parent, declared, and child ResourceSlot sets; child visibility is exactly the declared subset and does not imply a ResourceHandle or authorization.
SCOPE preserves child dimensions and ownership; missing authority/budget ceilings remain Unproven and child settlement before owner terminal RequiresEvidence.
COMPENSATION_SCOPE preserves Forward Effects, typed outcomes, and Forward Usage; potential compensation is additional and never refunds or rewrites the Forward history.

Only exact full RecoveryActionIdentity and RecoveryUsageBinding sources contribute; checked forward-occurrence, activation, and attempt bounds produce a conditional new Effect with zero lower bound, and the summed K upper must fit the exact declared action Effect occurrence.
Recovery Usage remains separate and is checked against potential action bounds; receipt eligibility and multi-event committed order require evidence, and RecoveryBlocked is not a business Failure.

Workflow-root derivation resolves all reachable leaves and accounts for every checked owned computation, known Effect occurrence/residual, and Recovery source exactly once in semantic order without promoting child obligations.
A root derived summary is not an exported ComponentContract; without a frozen root pin and cross-coordinate mapping, export compatibility remains NotExpressedInSemanticIr and Unproven.
Root Recovery closure compares the complete source, action-binding, forward-occurrence, and exact Usage-profile multisets; source-node coverage alone cannot prove action/profile accounting.

LocalActionBound and RootActionBound are distinct coordinates; exact caller/control-node/kind multiplicity identities are applied once with checked arithmetic and physical attempts are not multiplied twice.

Root Recovery uses operator-specific Effect/Usage algebra, retains typed control-path and validator-created guard evidence separately, keeps both action kinds and RACE losers, and assigns each action to its nearest CompensationScope or typed RootRecovery owner.
The root K action projection, including a same-atom Forward opportunity exactly once, must fit the already derived root epsilon ceiling and is never added as a second epsilon declaration.

Root K-required Recovery Usage must fit exact root U.recovery meter coordinates without double addition; missing active-source meters are not zero, overflow is a Violation, and runtime eligibility remains evidence-dependent.
The assertion pins the exact SemanticIrDigest and checked exported ComponentContractDigest.
The proof-context manifest commits the complete typed static universes, relation content, and resolver pins.
Compiler semantics identity includes exact normative content, applied RuleIds, and checker semantics version.
Root inputs require a complete bijection to exported input ports with exact nominal types and checked use sites.
Every exported output maps to an exact named WorkflowOutput with checked producer and nominal type evidence.
Root resources map through exact ResourceSlot and exported requirement-port identities.
Possible root business failures are contained by the exact exported nominal failure row.
Root effects and K action possibilities fit the exported epsilon ceiling after exact coordinate mapping.
Root information flow does not relax the exported flow restrictions; unknown influence is retained.
Root forward and recovery usage remain within separate exact exported phase, meter, unit, and bound coordinates.
Root recovery sources, actions, profiles, and safety declarations are compared without invented enum ordering.
Every child execution source meets exported feasibility and security constraints independently.
Subflow target pins do not prove implementation or body conformance.
Static compatibility does not establish authority, budget reservation, or runtime authorization.
A SpecificationId is unique across the Specification Registry; duplicate entries are a registry error.

Every registered normative source exists at a safe repo-relative path and its ArtifactFileDigest (plain SHA-256 of file bytes) matches; an ArtifactFileDigest is repository tooling identity and never a HashV1 DigestRef.
A frozen specification's normative source carries no provisional status marker.
The Usage Signature is a static declaration of additive upper bounds only: it is not a measurement, estimate, evidence, billing record, ledger reservation or runtime authorization.

A usage meter is resolved by the exact (catalog SpecificationId, NFC name) identity in an explicit read-only UsageMeterUniverse; unknown identities fail closed and no discovery or latest fallback exists.
This phase supports only non-negative integer additive meters with an explicit unit identity; unsupported aggregation is rejected and different units are not combined or treated as compatible.
Forward and recovery are independent (phase, meter) coordinates; recovery usage never refunds, overwrites or substitutes for forward usage.
finite(0), finite(n), unbounded and missing are distinct states; missing is never interpreted as finite(0), and unbounded is never encoded as UINT64_MAX.
Canonical Usage Signature form resolves meters, rejects duplicate (phase, meter) keys, orders by phase number and complete meter identity bytes, and is idempotent without deleting zero limits.
Additive accumulation is checked and conservative: finite bounds add, unbounded absorbs, and an unknown operand remains unknown; overflow never wraps or saturates.
Mutually exclusive branch join takes the maximum possible upper bound and is commutative, associative and idempotent; absent or unknown coordinates are not zero branches.
Finite repetition uses checked multiplication; repeat(0, U) produces explicit zero only for coordinates represented by U, and an unproven count cannot produce a false finite bound.
Static ceiling and compatibility judgments distinguish Proven, Unproven and Violation; inability to prove a bound is never reinterpreted as compatibility or zero usage.
Static control propagation is conservative: SEQUENCE and PARALLEL accumulate, SELECT joins, SCOPE preserves usage, TIMEOUT does not erase already possible usage, and AWAIT does not invent zero.
RETRY amplifies metered usage by maximum attempts, RACE retains loser usage, and ITERATE uses only a proven total repetition bound; max_inflight is never a total iteration count.

Usage non-increase compares the same phase, meter identity and unit; lower or equal finite ceilings and finite under old unbounded are Proven, while higher or newly unbounded ceilings are Violation and missing or incomparable coordinates are Unproven.
Usage quantity is not monetary cost; this phase has no currency, price snapshot, conversion, rounding or provider-pricing ABI.
A static ceiling proof is not a BudgetReservation, Reserve, Settle, Quota Ledger or cross-run quota decision; runtime ledgers remain separate authorities.
The Usage wire model and crate contain no receipt, ledger, runtime measurement, scheduler, worker, pricing API, policy engine or UsageSignatureDigest, and no HashV1 domain is added.
Currency identity and atomic unit are explicit universe-resolved values; currencies never imply precision or FX and incompatible currencies cannot be combined.
MoneyAmount is a non-negative uint64 atomic-unit count; floating point money, negative refunds and implicit conversions are absent.
PriceTableSnapshot is complete by value, immutable for this proof, and validates every meter and unit against explicit universes; no latest provider lookup exists.
Only fixed non-negative rational rates with denominator > 0 are supported; tiered and progressive pricing cannot be approximated as exact cost projection.
The supported safe rounding rule is per-meter-unit integer ceil; aggregate-once rounding is rejected because it can underestimate per-request upward rounding.
Every explicit possible Usage coordinate requires a matching price entry; missing price coverage is Unproven and never free.
Static Cost Projection preserves finite, unbounded and unproven states, forward/recovery coordinates and checked arithmetic; no missing or unknown usage becomes zero.
Forward and recovery static cost ceilings are checked independently; forward surplus cannot subsidize recovery overspend, and the result is not reservation or admission.
Cost non-increase is independent from Usage non-increase and is comparable only under equal Currency and equal complete price snapshot values.
Cost consumes the Phase 4A.5A Usage Envelope; it does not recount RACE, RETRY, FOREACH, HANDLE, compensation or TIMEOUT independently and does not invent zero for unresolved INVOKE/CALL_SUBFLOW.
Cost Projection adds no price snapshot digest, cost digest, budget digest or HashV1 domain and contains no billing, ledger, provider, FX, reservation, settlement, scheduler or runtime object.

specifications.description: Component identity and digest scope, exact public port ABI, cross-dimension static proof, typed K-to-epsilon guard compatibility, and substitution limits.
Closed thirteen-field ComponentContract ABI using exact pins to the existing semantic dimension schemas.
Exact versioned relation catalog snapshots and content-bound static proof assumptions.
Pure in-process RootExportAssertion proof: exact typed coordinates and nine-dimension static root/export compatibility, with body, publisher, authority, budget and runtime evidence kept separate.
The AFIDL1 builtin machine primitive universe expressed as a parseable nominal-alias module; its 13 alias digests are frozen in the AFIDL corpus.
Closed central registry of HashV1 digest domains.
HashV1 digest foundation: exact formula, SHA-256 only, DigestRef and the domain separation invariant.
Exact operation/resource-type compatibility relation, selector mappings and complete qualifier profiles.

Effect Signature semantics: the declaration/authorization boundary, atom identity, fail-closed catalog resolution, occurrence bound and guard rules, the closed/open/top row distinction, the effect algebra (containment, accumulation, branch join, repetition) and static control-opcode propagation.

Normative shape of the Effect Signature: effect atoms (operation identity, logical resource selector, closed qualifiers), explicit occurrence bounds, the closed guard language and the four capability row states (pure, closed, bounded-open, unknown). Reuses the semantic core's PrimitiveConstant by exact cross-module import.
ACE1: the deterministic, schema-directed, UTF-8 canonical encoding of AgentFlow values (strict JSON subset).

Static X semantics: hard/soft separation, explicit capability/profile universes, canonicalization, descriptor matching, separate feasibility and security-preservation proofs, compatibility and the no-authority boundary.

Normative shape of static Execution Requirements: exact capability and attribute requirements, independent nominal compute quantities, sandbox, trust, region/residency, runtime profile, implementation ABI obligations and closed soft preferences.

Failure Row semantics: the six error planes, nominal identity and exact pinning, the closed-row and empty-not-success rules, canonical ordering, exact containment, the union algebra, HANDLE residual and handler propagation, control propagation, and the Unproven analysis result.

Normative shape of the static Typed Failure Row: the nominal FailureTypeRef (an exact TypeSchemaRef pin reused from the semantic core) and the closed FailureRow set. Only typed business failures enter the row; control outcomes, recovery states, infrastructure facts and incidents are structurally outside it.
Exact information-flow and execution region, trust, sandbox and sink relation.
Closed normative table of the AFIDL1 builtin primitive universe.

AFIDL1: the closed schema definition language, its grammar, its identity model and (Phase 2C) its cross-module import capability. Imports are an additive AFIDL1 source feature: the language major stays 1 and every module without imports keeps its exact previous meaning and digests.
The canonical TypeSchema machine representation and the TypeSchemaDigest identity formula (sections 6-7 of the AFIDL1 grammar).

Information Flow semantics: the four-concept separation (provenance/trust/taint/flow), the frozen security invariants, label and taint identity, instruction authority with no self-elevation, conservative may-influence propagation, the LLM strong taint mixer, the egress/influence split, declassification/endorsement obligations, persistence without trust upgrade, unknown handling, flow non-relaxation and the static-vs-runtime boundary.

Normative shape of the static Information Flow Contract: confidentiality and taint labels as separate nominal types, the closed instruction-authority scale, typed logical source categories, the conservative static influence summary, data-egress vs decision-influence flow kinds, workflow-output and structured effect-operation sinks, and the closed flow contract. The external effect sink reuses the effect signature's EffectOperationRef by exact cross-module import.

Static Recovery semantics: replay boundaries, idempotency declarations, unknown and partial effect safety, reconciliation/compensation obligations, forward-history preservation, static proofs and conservative compatibility.

Normative shape of the static Recovery Contract: replay and idempotency semantics, key obligations, exact EffectAtom recovery clauses, reconciliation requirements, unknown-effect handling and compensation obligations.
Exhaustive exact recovery-action to usage-meter coverage catalog.
Registry mechanics: Specification Registry, RuleId system, Stable ABI Number Registry, ConformanceCaseId and canonical registry form.
Closed table of RuleId areas.

Resource Requirement semantics: nominal identity and exact pinning, the explicit resource-type universe, the requirement port namespace, exact-value attributes, the closed row, canonical ordering, static satisfaction, requirement non-strengthening, the Unproven result, the requirement/capability/grant distinction and the deferred binding/handle boundary.

Normative shape of the static Resource Requirement Row: the nominal ResourceTypeRef (an exact TypeSchemaRef pin reused from the semantic core), the exact-value ResourceAttributeConstraint, the port-keyed ResourceRequirement and the closed ResourceRequirementRow. Only static need is declared here; binding, handles, adapters and authority are structurally outside.
Derived-only static propagation for existing ITERATE, RETRY, TIMEOUT and HANDLE opcodes without changing Semantic IR or ComponentContract ABI.
Conservative, provenance-preserving static composition for SEQUENCE, SELECT, PARALLEL and RACE without workflow ABI or runtime authority.
Normative shape of the workflow semantic core: primitive universe, semantic type DAG, digest-pinned references, value slots, pure expressions and logical resource slots.
Canonical Semantic IR semantics: static scope, ownership tree, value producer rules, interface equality, per-opcode static schemas, canonical ordering and the SemanticIrDigest.

Normative shape of the canonical Semantic IR: the closed 13-opcode computation set, structured ownership, run parameters, workflow outputs, the closed contract table and the SemanticIrDocument. The first production consumer of the AFIDL1 cross-module import.
Exact, source-preserving static contract resolution for INVOKE, AWAIT and CALL_SUBFLOW computation leaves; no workflow control algebra or runtime authority.

Derived-only SCOPE and COMPENSATION_SCOPE algebra, checked full control-tree closure, and root-relative K action/Recovery-Usage proof with runtime authority, receipts, export assertions, reservations, and execution explicitly outside this static proof boundary.
Workflow semantic core semantics: machine vs workflow primitives, type DAG rules, exact pinning, SSA value slots, expression purity and type checking, resource slot scope.
Normative shape of the Specification, Rule and ABI-number registries (self-hosting bootstrap module).

Static Cost Projection semantics: currency identity, atomic units, fixed rational pricing, conservative per-meter-unit rounding, meter coverage, static cost and budget proofs, cost non-increase and the runtime billing boundary.
Normative shape of the static Cost Projection declaration: explicit currency and atomic money, rational fixed price entries, immutable price table snapshot and forward/recovery static cost ceiling.

Static Usage semantics: explicit meter universe and units, additive upper bounds, phase separation, canonicalization, conservative usage algebra and control propagation, static ceiling proof, non-increase compatibility and the runtime ledger boundary.
Normative shape of the static Usage Signature: exact additive meter identity, forward/recovery phases, finite/unbounded upper bounds and the closed Usage Signature declaration.
